title: Disney President Dana Walden Addresses Future of ABC's Jimmy Kimmel Live | Entertainment
text:
Disney President Dana Walden calls late night a challenging daypart as she discusses the future of Jimmy Kimmel's show on ABC amid contract talks.
Disney President Dana Walden said it is a very challenging daypart when asked on Thursday about the future of ABC's Jimmy Kimmel Live, which was briefly suspended last year after host Jimmy Kimmel's shocking remarks about the assassination of Charlie Kirk. Kimmel is currently on a one-year contract for his talk show on ABC, which is owned by Disney.
Challenges in Late Night Television
Walden explained that the late night time slot faces significant challenges. She noted that while Jimmy Kimmel is doing a phenomenal job and his ratings are up, they are up relative to a smaller audience that is watching late night on broadcast television. This context is important as the network evaluates the show's performance.
She also pointed out that having a strong online presence is not a lucrative opportunity for a very premium talk show. On-air advertising generates far more revenue than views and clicks from social media platforms. This financial reality adds to the complexity of the situation.
Contract Negotiations and Business Considerations
Walden emphasized that the network is trying to make sense of the business while honoring a deep partnership with Kimmel. She expressed affection for him, stating that she loves Jimmy and they have a great friendship, and he is close to a number of people at Disney. These personal ties are part of the ongoing discussions.
The Disney president added that they are working through the situation to understand what Jimmy wants, what the right thing to do is, and what is right for the business. This process involves balancing creative and commercial factors.
Future of the Show Beyond 2026
Kimmel's contract could continue through the 2026-27 season, leaving the show's longer-term future open and unclear. The suspension last year following his remarks about the Charlie Kirk assassination added a layer of controversy that the network has had to navigate.
As ABC and Disney weigh their options, the decision will impact the late night lineup and the network's overall strategy. The outcome of these negotiations will be closely watched by industry observers and fans alike.
